column2: Sharpless's asymmetric dihydroxylation, part of his 2001 Nobel Prize, sold as a ready-made powder: AD-mix-α or AD-mix-β, depending on which mirror image you want. Just add your alkene.
So reactive it sets fire to sand, glass and asbestos, and an infamous entry in Derek Lowe's "Things I Won't Work With". That fame makes it a much more common answer than it sounds.
